question: By what name was the administrative head of the Mauryan city administration, as described in the Arthashastra, addressed?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Nagarika__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nagarika was the chief administrative officer of a city in the Mauryan period.
 
• Mentioned in Kautilya’s Arthashastra as responsible for urban administration.
 
• Duties included law and order, sanitation, trade regulation, and revenue collection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gop**

 
 
• Gopa/Gop was a rural administrative official, not an urban authority.
 
• Responsible for supervising villages and groups of households.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Mauryan Administration:**
 
 
• Centralized Power: Emperor held ultimate authority, advised by a Council of Ministers (Mantriparishad).
 
• Bureaucracy: A vast, hierarchical system with senior officials like Tirthas (18 top officials) and Adhyakshyas (superintendents for various departments).
 
• Provincial Administration: Empire divided into provinces (e.g., Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali) governed by royal princes or governors (Kumaras, Rajukas).
 
• Military Strength: Maintained a massive army (infantry, cavalry, elephants, navy) under a board of 30 officers, essential for defense and control.
 
• Revenue & Economy: Revenue from agriculture, trade, and taxes; strong focus on trade routes, weights, and measures.
 
• Judiciary: King as head, with courts like Dharmasthiya (civil) and Kantakashodhana (criminal), plus local judges.
